newsitem.title: USA: Clinton promises to help St. Petersburg rebuild.
newsitem.headline: Clinton promises to help St. Petersburg rebuild.

text.p: President Clinton promised federal assistance Tuesday to help St. Petersburg rebuild a minority neighbourhood damaged by fire during recent race riots and create jobs in the Florida city.

"We've had some recommendations for action that involve a real partnership among federal agencies, city officials and community leaders," Clinton said in a telephone call with St. Petersburg Mayor David Fischer.
"A federal coordinator who will report to the community empowerment board which is chaired by the vice president will be appointed to work on the ground with you in St. Petersburg," Clinton added.

The city was rocked by more than two dozen fires on the night of Oct. 24 after a white police officer shot and killed a black teenager in a predominantly black neighbourhood. The officer said the 18-year-old man tried to run him down with a car after a traffic stop.
Racial unrest flared anew last month after a grand jury decided not to indict the officer. He was suspended for 60 days by the police department.
Housing and Urban Development Secretary Henry Cisneros recently visited the city and recommended redevelopment plans to create jobs for minorities.
"I am confident that you can work through this," Clinton told Fischer.
Replied Fischer: "This is a community that meets its challenges and we're going to do this one and we're going to do it right."
Black leaders have asked the federal Civil Rights Commission to investigate race relations in the city.
